title: Leaving London for Brussels at Pollard's call
summary: After finishing the Murray's contract, Briggs, Hines and Morris decided to go to the continent when drummer Fitz-Pollard wired for musicians in Brussels, and Briggs sorts out the dates.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: continue. We did. We continued to the end of our contracts, and then the three of us, Bobo Hines, Lawrence Morris, and I, we decided to come over to France.
To come to France?
Yes.
Now, you were -- now, the Club, this is the same club that you'd been playing in?
Murray's Club.
Murray's Club?
Right.
So you then worked your contract out, so now it must have been about what, 1920.
'21 by this time, right.
No, it was '22, the spring of '22.
Briggs
So you had been really -- let me get this straight then. So, you had been gigging around London, for what, working since the middle of 19 --
The beginning of 1920 -- beginning of 1920, when the split happened.
Right.
We did that, because six months, six months, it goes fast.
Right. So this is now the beginning of 1921?
Right, yes.
So, you decided to go to Paris. Did you have anything lined up there?
I had a contract with Fitz-Pollard. Fitz-Pollard was a wonderful percussion-drummer, from Chicago. And he worked in Brussels with Mistinquet. He was at the Alhambra Theater in
Briggs
Brussels, and Pericay Cabaret, owned by Mr. Leon Voltera who had the Casino de Paris in Paris.

And he sent a wire, he needed musicians. He wired. I got a wire from him. And Patrick, who was elsewhere, he got a wire from him. Both of us. We both went to Brussels to join his orchestra. finish the (inaudible) in spring.
In other words you-- all of you guys were pretty well known, I guess.
That is what happened, the Europeans knew about you and it was easy to get work there?
